description: Cross-host on-disk credential format and state contract. Every host (Node, Rust, Go, C#) must reproduce these values byte-for-byte and classify these states identically.

aclSamples.description: 0600: readable and writable by the owner only.
0400: read-only for the owner, which is still owner-only.
0640: the owning group can read the secret.
0644: every account on the machine can read the secret.
0666: every account can read and rewrite the secret.

states.description: No datastore and no secrets file: the first run of a new install.
A valid secrets file is reused unchanged, on an install that already has a datastore.
A datastore written before per-install credentials has no secrets file. The host must report that migration is required instead of handing out a usable password.
The secrets file is not parseable JSON. It must be reported and left untouched, not rewritten.
The secrets file is valid JSON but carries no usable surrealPassword field.
The stored value carries the obfuscation prefix but its payload is not valid base64.
The stored value decodes to the empty string, which cannot be a password.
The stored value contains a control character, which cannot survive a process environment or a CLI argument.
The secrets file exists and its ACL cannot be established as owner-only. The secret may already be exposed, so startup must stop instead of continuing.
The datastore path exists but cannot be inspected, so the host cannot tell a fresh install from a legacy one.
